headlines.summary: Apple announces a new touchscreen laptop, the company's third major launch under new CEO John Ternus.
headlines.article_text: MacBook Pro: Apple brings touch to the Mac Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apple announced its first laptop with a touchscreen will go on sale Nov. 6. The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. Global PC shipments have fallen and Apple faces pressure from rising memory costs and higher computer prices. Touchscreens have not typically driven laptop purchases, making Apple's software changes and developer strategy central to whether the feature catches on. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT German-Russian record producer and DJ Zedd, at left, and Apple CEO John Ternus look at the new M6 14-inch MacBook Pro during the Apple Experience LA event in Los Angeles, Oct. 28, 2026. Frederic J. Brown | Afp | Getty Images Apple on Wednesday announced its first laptop with a touchscreen, which it's calling MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display. Apple said the laptop has a new display, using OLED technology, that offers more brightness, better colors and wider viewing angles. It's using Apple's M5 Pro or Max chips, and Apple said Wednesday that it's lighter than Apple's current Pro laptops. It's still an Apple laptop, and is running MacOS, not a version of the iPhone or iPad operating system. In a video, Apple showed users swiping on the screen to manipulate videos or images. It also has a glowing Apple logo on the laptop's lid. The new laptop will go on sale Nov. 6 and the 14-inch version will start at $2,899. The 16-inch version will cost at least $3,399. Both are notable price increases from existing models. This is Apple's third major product launch under new CEO John Ternus, signaling a faster cadence for hardware releases. It's also a major reversal for Apple, which has resisted putting touchscreens on its laptops for decades as some Windows machines gained the feature. "Yes, for the very first time, we are bringing touch to the Mac," Ternus said in live remarks to media and analysts in Los Angeles. The laptop market has been going through one of its worst slumps ever. Overall shipments are expected to be down 11% this year. Analysts say the AI-driven global market shortage of memory has contributed to higher laptop prices, which has hurt sales and demand. In the third quarter, total PC shipments dropped 20% on a year-over-year basis, according to market researcher IDC. Apple's own shipments fell 11% during the quarter, according to the estimate. Attendees try out the new touchscreen MacBook Pro during the Apple Experience LA in Los Angeles, Oct. 28, 2026. Frederic J. Brown | AFP | Getty Images Even Apple's not immune to rising memory prices, after then-CEO Tim Cook warned this summer that the situation around memory prices was "unsustainable." Nearly all Macs got price hikes this year. Mac Minis introduced in August got a $300 bump, for example. The announcement caps a busy two months of product launches under Ternus. Apple also introduced new iMac and MacBook Pro models with M6 chips this week, after price hikes to the lineup totaling several hundred dollars in June. Apple introduced an iPad Mini on Monday that starts at $699, $100 more than its predecessor. In September, Apple released new iPhones, including its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo. It also revealed a new smart speaker with a display called HomeView that uses a redesigned version of Siri to answer a broader range of questions. The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. In the most recent quarter, Apple reported $10.35 billion in Mac sales, or just under 10% of the company's total revenue. But many software developers swear by the Mac, and it remains the only supported platform to develop iPhone apps. And in recent months, Apple has highlighted its chips and memory architecture to make the case that its computers are the best fit for local or edge AI that runs on a device, instead of the cloud. Meta's AI model developer team bought hundreds of Mac Minis this year to test agents, for example. And Apple notably teamed up with Meta earlier this month to make an announcement that large, nearly frontier models can run on clusters of Macs connected with high-speed cabling, allowing developers to run agentic code without paying Anthropic or OpenAI. Read more CNBC tech news Amazon’s anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI Chart: Anthropic’s cash pile towers over nearly every U.S. company Google alters its cloud playbook, enlisting partners to sell more AI chips A guide to some of the biggest risks in Anthropic's IPO prospectus Apple has had a historical resistance to touchscreen laptops. Software chief Craig Federighi said in 2018 that the ergonomics would fatigue users. "We make the world's best touch computer on an iPad," Ternus, then Apple's senior VP of hardware engineering, told The Wall Street Journal in 2021. "It's totally optimized for that. And the Mac is totally optimized for indirect input. We haven't really felt a reason to change that." Ternus has been working on Macs since he joined the company and was credited along with silicon chief Johny Srouji as the leader of Apple's effort to get Macs running on Apple's chips, not Intel's. Apple credited Ternus' work on Mac in its official CEO transition statement . That may be why Ternus in his early days as CEO will be the executive to backtrack on a long-running Apple design philosophy. Touchscreen laptops have been available on Windows machines for a long time, but they're just another feature, not a selling point behind most purchasing decisions, said Ryan Reith, IDC's vice president for worldwide device trackers. Only 17% of notebook PCs shipped globally this year will have touchscreens, according to IDC data. Touchscreen laptops also have a slightly lower average selling price than non-touchscreen notebooks. Hardware technology hasn't been the limiting factor for Apple merging its desktop and mobile interfaces, he added, and Apple could have been waiting to launch a touchscreen laptop until it could present a good user experience and perfect its software after attempts to make its iPad more like a laptop. "This is really a user interface and software thing," Reith said. "It's one more thing that can draw the developers in." watch now VIDEO 1:16 01:16 First Wall Street checks show iPhone Duo demand holding despite early display issues Closing Bell Choose CNBC as your preferred source on Google and never miss a moment from the most trusted name in business news.

Michael Wayland / CNBC Shares of Stellantis were up Wednesday as the European car giant's third-quarter results showed it was making progress with its 60 billion euro turnaround plan. Third-quarter revenues rose 1% to 37.6 billion euros from a year ago, the Chrysler and Jeep owner said on Wednesday, while adjusted operating income rose 184% to 256 million euros from 90 million euros a year earlier. The automaker's industrial free cash flow improved to negative 4 billion euros, up from negative 4.3 billion the year prior. Stellantis on Wednesday also reconfirmed its 2026 guidance and target to achieve positive free cash flow next year, which is a main focus for investors. "Q3 was soft, but consensus expectations were far lower. Key here is that '26 Guidance was maintained while other auto OEMs and suppliers are cutting on elevated costs," RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan said Wednesday in an investor note. Stellantis stock on the New York Stock Exchange rose 13% on Wednesday to close at $4.69 a share. Shares in Milan closed at 4.28 euros, up 15.4%. Shares in both markets remain sharply down since the beginning of the year. Stellantis stock since the beginning of the year. Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa told investors Wednesday that the company is ahead of schedule on its turnaround plan, which was announced in May. He said Stellantis expects to exceed its previously announced cost-cutting efforts of 6 billion euros under the plan by 2028, including 2.4 billion euros to start 2027. "We are very confident in reaffirming our '26 guidance. Those include '27 free cash flow positive," Filosa said Wednesday in response to concerns about the carmaker's ability to achieve its free cash flow target. Stellantis' 2026 guidance includes a mid-single-digit percentage increase in net revenue and a low-single-digit adjusted operating margin. Stellantis' turnaround plan includes investing 36 billion euros in its portfolio of automotive brands, with 60% of the cash to go towards its struggling North America sector. It also plans to introduce new vehicles, refresh models, and incorporate new technologies in its products. Stellantis is targeting roughly 23% revenue growth, from 154 billion euros last year to 190 billion euros by 2030, with a 7% adjusted operating margin by then. China competition European carmakers, including Stellantis, have been struggling in China as domestic brands like Xiaomi, BYD and Geely gain ground and intensify competition. Just this week, German luxury carmaker Porsche said it would reduce its exposure to China as car sales decline in the region. headlines.article_text: Three media outlets seek full White House access in amended lawsuit Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points MS NOW, CNN and Politico, in an amended lawsuit, asked a judge to order that they be allowed to serve as press pool for areas in the White House such as the Oval Office, as well as on Air Force One. President Trump banned the media outlets from the White House in September, but a federal judge soon afterward ordered that they be readmitted there. The outlets say the White House has continued to prevent them from coverage certain areas of the complex. The amended complaint sets the stage for a court fight over whether a president, because of how he or she feels about how a media outlet covers them, can block access to individual media outlets or reporters from areas of the White House that other journalists have access to. In this article VSNT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT U.S. President Donald Trump stops to speak to members of the media as he departs on the South Lawn of the White House on Oct. 22, 2026 in Washington, DC. Alex Wong | Getty Images Three media outlets that President Donald Trump banned from the White House in September, only to have a federal judge's order restore much of their access, amended their lawsuit Wednesday, seeking to regain full access to serve in a press pool for other reporters in the Oval Office and Air Force One . The amended civil complaint against Trump says that since the judge ordered the White House to allow MS NOW , CNN and Politico journalists into the White House, the White House has blocked those outlets from performing pool functions they long have conducted. The press pool routinely serves as a key source of information for the public about what a president does or says. In pool assignments, journalists agree to share with other media outlets information and images they obtain while acting as a pooler. The amended complaint sets the stage for a court fight over whether a president, because of how he or she feels about how a media outlet covers them, can block access to individual media outlets or reporters from areas of the White House that other journalists have access to. Ted Boutrous Jr., an attorney for the outlets, in a statement Wednesday said, "Despite two court orders restraining it from implementing the President's unconstitutional ban on CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO, the White House has continued to violate the First Amendment and due process by excluding those news organizations from areas such as the Oval Office and Air Force One — the very locations that the President most frequently engages with the press." "These exclusions, intended to punish and chill coverage of the administration that the President doesn't like, make it harder for the press to cover some of the most important events in the world for the benefit of the American people," Boutrous said. The amended complaint in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C. says that Trump's original ban and "the White House's continued exclusion of Plaintiffs from certain [areas] are unlawful retaliation for protected First Amendment activity." Those actions "brazenly" discriminate against the outlets "based on their perceived editorial viewpoint; the White House is expressly excluding CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO because the President dislikes the content of their coverage," the suit says. Judge Tim Kelly's prior orders restoring access for the outlets did not require the White House to restore those outlets' access to the Oval Office or Air Force One. The amended complaint notes that since his second term began in January 2025, Trump has held 121 press events aboard Air Force One or on the tarmac outside the presidential plane, and 138 events in the Oval Office, "during which he fielded no fewer than 4,700 questions from reporters." "To be clear, Plaintiffs do not claim an unrestricted right to enter the Oval Office or travel aboard Air Force One," the new complaint says. "But once the White House opens those spaces to selected journalists for newsgathering and reporting, the White House may not exclude Plaintiffs because it dislikes their coverage." Members of the media report from Pebble Beach, the stand-up area for members of the media on the North Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. Al Drago | Bloomberg | Getty Images Since Trump announced the ban on Sept. 18, "the White House has repeatedly barred CNN from fulfilling its duties as designated television network pooler aboard Air Force One — a role CNN has fulfilled for more than four decades," the amended suit says. MS NOW has not participated in the secondary TV pool since that date, and the White House has barred Politico "from two scheduled out-of-town print pool assignments aboard Air Force One," the suit says. "Defendants have offered no official explanation for any of these exclusions," the amended complaint says. "Indeed, the President has been explicit that he intends to limit access to the Oval Office to news organizations that cover him favorably, declaring hours after this action was filed that 'publications that only write negatively . . . shouldn't be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World," the suit said. The suit notes that after Kelly issued a preliminary injunction against Trump's ban in mid-October, "the White House issued a statement declaring that what it deems the 'Fake News' has 'no place demanding a spot in the President's Oval Office.'" President Donald Trump speaks with reporters on the South Lawn of the White House before boarding Marine One en route to Alaska on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Tom Williams | Cq-roll Call, Inc. | Getty Images The amended complaint says the limited ban on pool access violates the Due Process Clause of the U.S. Constitution. "CNN, MS NOW, POLITICO, and their journalists have liberty and property interests in their press credentials and the access those credentials afford to the White House grounds to report on the President and his administration," the suit says. "That access has long extended to the Oval Office, Air Force One, and other fora that the White House has opened to the press for pool coverage." "The ban, and Defendants' continued exclusion of Plaintiffs from certain White House press areas, deprives Plaintiffs of those interests without meeting the bare minimum requirements of due process: advance notice based on clear standards and an opportunity to be heard," the suit says. The suit also said the White House is interfering with CNN's ability to perform its duties as one of five television networks that "staff, equip, and bear the costs associated with the primary television network pool upon which the American public (and the White House itself) relies for real-time television coverage of the President in the Oval Office, aboard Air Force One, and at the many other presidential events that due to size and other constraints simply cannot accommodate all members of the press corps." Trump, when he announced the ban, said he was "sick" of what he called fiction and lies written about him, his administration, and the United States. headlines.article_text: Microsoft (MSFT) Q1 earnings report 2027 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Microsoft reported 19% revenue growth, topping estimates. Azure cloud revenue jumped 48% to $33.2 billion. Free cash flow declined 27% from a year ago. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella speaks at a company event at La Defense business district in Puteaux, near Paris, on Oct. 20, 2026. Dimitar Dilkoff | AFP | Getty Images Microsoft shares rose 5% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business. Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: $4.89 adjusted vs. $4.73 expected Revenue: $92.28 billion vs. $90.69 billion expected Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement . Net income of $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, increased from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, in the same quarter of last year. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million impact from investing in OpenAI. Free cash flow of $18.63 billion moved 27% lower. Cloud rival Alphabet showed negative free cash flow for the quarter, while Meta said last week that it went free cash flow negative . Microsoft has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to accommodate artificial intelligence demand. The company had $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30%. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion. For the first time in an earnings statement, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $32.32 billion, which would have represented growth of more than 44%. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%. Microsoft reported results under two operating segments for the first time since 1998. For the past 11 years it had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses. Agents and Infra gave Microsoft $76.80 billion of its revenue, which was up almost 25% and more than the $75.63 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. The segment contains Azure, along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services. Revenue from Microsoft 365 cloud services came to $27.78 billion, above the $27.37 billion consensus. The other new segment, Devices and Consumer, contributed $15.48 billion in revenue, down 3% but higher than StreetAccount's consensus of $15.05 billion. It includes search and advertising, Xbox, devices and Windows operating system licenses sold to device makers. Microsoft said sales of devices and Windows licenses declined 22%. Industry researcher Gartner said PC shipments during the quarter slid 22% as higher memory and storage costs elevated prices. As of Wednesday's close, Microsoft shares were up about 10% year to date, trailing the S&P 500 index, which has gained 13% over the same period. During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft said it would cut 4,800 jobs , and followed up by announcing on Monday that it's offering buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, as it strives to balance a costly AI build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft also established, during the quarter, an AI implementation unit and revealed a Copilot AI "super app" with coding abilities. This story is developing. Please check back for updates. The Detroit automaker also narrowed its 2026 guidance, raising it at the low end, and said earnings next year will be in line with its results from this year. Charles-McClintock Wilson | Nurphoto | Getty Images DETROIT — Ford Motor expects earnings next year will be roughly in line with the automaker's anticipated results this year, the company said Wednesday as it reported mixed results for the third quarter. The Detroit automaker beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations but slightly missed revenue estimates. The company has been working to stabilize production of its F-Series pickup trucks after dealing with supplier issues for much of the past year. "This quarter's results reflect deliberate actions to improve profitability and deliver consistent financial returns," Ford CFO Sherry House told reporters during a call Wednesday. Here's how Ford performed in the third quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: 49 cents adjusted vs. 40 cents expected Automotive revenue: $46.08 billion vs. $46.24 billion expected The Detroit automaker also narrowed its 2026 guidance to adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $10.5 billion and $11 billion, compared with a previous outlook of $10 billion to $11 billion. Ford maintained its adjusted free cash flow guidance for this year of between $6 billion and $7 billion. House also said the company expects 2027 profitability to be roughly in line with this year's results, citing several offsetting factors in production issues this year as well as rising commodity costs. House noted a $1.3 billion tariff refund during the first quarter of this year was largely offset by additional costs from alternative aluminum sourcing that the company does not expect to have next year, leveling out the year-over-year comparison. She also said production of its F-Series Super Duty trucks in Canada in 2027 will make up for lost production it's expecting at its F-150 factories to retool for new models. "Next year will be the third year on our journey of increasing and improving our warranty and material cost savings, and that's getting extended to structural costs throughout the company as well in terms of savings," House said. Ahead of the results, Wall Street analysts were mixed about whether Ford would be able to maintain profits in 2027. The company has multiple efforts that will add to costs next year: It's rolling out several new or redesigned models, including its next-generation EV and Canada-produced pickups, and is enhancing its energy business that it announced earlier this year. The missed revenue for the third quarter was a result of each of the automaker's main business units – which are broken into Blue traditional operations, Pro fleet and Model e electric vehicle segments – underperforming compared with Wall Street's expectations, according to StreetAccount. As part of its modified guidance, Ford said it now expects pre-tax earnings of its Ford Blue unit to be $5.5 billion, which is at the high end of a previous guidance. It's also anticipating EBIT of about $7 billion for the year for Ford Pro and Ford Model e losses of about $4 billion. Its Ford Credit unit is expected to record about $2.8 billion in EBIT for 2026. Ford's overall revenue, which includes its credit segment, was off roughly 2% compared with the third quarter of last year, to $49.5 billion. Its net income also was off $400 million from a year earlier to $2 billion, while adjusted earnings before interest and taxes were up slightly year-over-year to $2.7 billion. Ford's 2025 third-quarter results included $47.19 billion in automotive revenue, net income of $2.4 billion and earnings per share of 45 cents adjusted. CNBC Oracle shares jumped 11% on Wednesday after the software company issued a revenue forecast of $225 billion for fiscal 2030, implying 35% average annual growth, and said it will limit additional fundraising over that stretch to $20 billion. At its investor day, Oracle said that, as part of its financing plan for fiscal 2027 through 2030, the amount raised will be divided equally between equity and debt. "Vendor financing, customer-provided hardware and customer prepayments are expected to reduce upfront cash requirements through the transition to positive free cash flow," Oracle said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Analysts polled by LSEG expected revenue growth of 8% in fiscal 2027, followed by significant acceleration over the next two years. They're projecting revenue in fiscal 2030 of $224.2 billion. Prior to Wednesday, Oracle had lost about one-third of its value this year on concern that rising interest rates and the company's hefty debt load will make its artificial intelligence buildout too costly. Oracle has issued $117 billion in long-term debt and is clinging to an investment-grade credit rating of BBB-, the lowest level of investment grade above junk, according to S&P. Long known as a giant in enterprise software, Oracle jumped into the AI infrastructure game in a major way last year to try and compete with the hyperscalers like Google and Amazon while providing capacity to OpenAI. Its capital expenditures more than doubled to $55.7 billion in fiscal 2026, and are expected to jump another 65% this fiscal year to $91.9 billion, according to FactSet. Oracle needs revenue expansion from its buildout to cover the soaring costs. The company said its operating margin in fiscal 2030 will top 40%. Oracle also said it will turn free cash flow positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 and reach more than $30 billion in free cash flow the following year. Analysts expect negative free cash flow of $35 billion this fiscal year and a similar number next year, according to FactSet. The spread on Oracle's five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, currently sits at 277 basis points after reaching about 320 basis points earlier this month. It's up almost 100% this year. —CNBC's Michelle Fox and Jordan Novet contributed to this report. headlines.article_text: FTC demands Walmart and others hand over data on personalized pricing Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Andrew Ferguson speaks during the Semafor World Economy Summit 2025 at Conrad Washington on April 23, 2025 in Washington, DC. Kayla Bartkowski | Getty Images The Federal Trade Commission is demanding information from Walmart , Uber and seven other companies on whether and how they use consumers' personal data such as location, browsing history and income to set individual prices, wages and job offers, a senior FTC official told Reuters on Wednesday. The FTC is flexing its consumer protection powers ahead of the U.S. congressional elections next week, as voters consistently rank the cost of living as the most important issue. Target , along with app services Lyft , DoorDash and Instacart, and airlines Delta , United , JetBlue , are also receiving demands, the official said. The FTC will use the information to eventually publish a study to help inform regulators and lawmakers about personalized pricing and wage setting practices. The advance of algorithmic pricing technology, including tools that incorporate AI, has fueled concern that companies are able to set prices for shoppers on an individual basis in order to extract the maximum price each shopper would be willing to pay. Personalized pricing strategies are difficult to observe from the outside, because they serve different prices to different people. The FTC study aims to fill in that knowledge gap, demanding comprehensive information about the tools, strategies, and data companies use as well as how they affect prices, wages and job offers. Efforts by state lawmakers to ban personalized pricing, along with the use of algorithms to individually tailor wages, have taken off in recent years. The National Retail Federation has criticized the laws and defended retailers' use of data-driven discounts as a means of incentivizing loyalty. FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson has said personalizing pricing could violate consumer protection laws where consumers do not expect it and that companies should expect enforcement. After the FTC called for public comment, hundreds of commenters urged the FTC to ban the practice outright. The FTC has said it does not have the authority to issue a blanket prohibition against the practice.
